MATTHEW.|81 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>vvould. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=16}}† And he had then a notorious prisoner, that vvas called Barabbas. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=17}}† They therfore being gathered together, Pilate said: whom vvil you that I release to you, Barabbas, or {{sc|Iesvs}} that is called Christ? {{verse|chapter=27|verse=18}}† For he knevve that for enuie they had deliuered him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=19}}† And as he vvas sitting in place of iudgment, his vvife sent vnto him, saying: Haue thou nothing to doe vvith that iust man. for I haue suffred many things this day in my sleepe for him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=20}}† But the cheefe Priestes and auncients persuaded the people, that they should aske Barabbas, and make {{sc|Iesvs}} avvay. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=21}}† And the President ansvvering, said to them: Whether vvil you of the tvvo to be released vnto you? But they said, Barabbas. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=22}}† Pilate saith to them, what shal I doe then vvith {{sc|Iesvs}} that is called Christ? They say al, Let him be crucified. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=23}}† The President said to them, why vvhat euil hath he done? But they cried the more, saying, Let him be crucified. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=24}}† And Pilate seeing that he nothing preuailed, but rather tumult vvas tovvard: taking vvater he vvashed his hands before the people, saying, I am {{sup|‖}} innocent of the bloud of this iust man: looke you to it. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=25}}† And the vvhole people ansvvering, said, His bloud be vpon vs, and vpon our children. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=26}}† Then he released to them Barabbas, and hauing scourged {{sc|Iesvs}}, deliuered him vnto them for to be crucified.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=27}}† Then the Presidents souldiars taking {{sc|Iesvs}} into the Palace, gathered together vnto him the vvhole band: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=28}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 19, 2.''}}* and stripping him, put a scarlet cloke about him, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=29}}† and platting a crovvne of thornes, put it vpon his head, and a reede in his right hand. And bovving the knee before him, they mocked him, saying, Haile King of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=30}}† And spitting vpon him, they tooke the reede, and smote his head. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=31}}† And after they had mocked him, they tooke of the cloke from him, and put on him his ovvne garments, and led him avvay to crucifie him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=32}}† And in going they found a man of Cyréne, named Simon: him they forced to take vp his crosse. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=33}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=HORA SEXTA in the Churches Seruice.}}And they came into the place that is called Golgotha, vvhich is, the place of Caluarie. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=34}}† And they gaue him vvine to drinke mingled vvith gall. And vvhen he had tasted, he vvould not drinke.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=35}}† And after they had crucified him, they deuided his garments, casting lottes: that it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas spoken by the Prophet, saying: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 21, 19.''}}''They deuided my garments among''<noinclude>{{rh||L|them:}}</noinclude>
